So I've been learning web development that last little while and was coming up with ideas for projects I could do, and one I came up with was a small notebook-like app that I can use to edit and store my notes. Being interested in so many different areas of tech has lead to a pretty sizable stack of notebooks on my desk, so in an attempt to get those off my desk, simplify the process of taking notes, and make it easier to go over my old notes, I figured digitizing my notes would be the next step in making my workflow more efficient. I wondered whether simply using OpenOffice writer might be more efficient, but so far I really like using DigiNotes. I've added a second monitor to my laptop that sits vertically so I can read my PDFs off the vertical monitor while using DigiNotes on my laptop screen, while using alt-tab to switch focus between the two.

Screenshots: https://sli.mg/a/HbJ70n

There's a few issues with it, however. Given that this was my first web dev project I pretty much built it as I learned so the code (especially the CSS and JavaScript) is pretty messy. Also, I don't have a hosting account so if you wanted to run this you would have to set up a local server on your machine, with the PHP and MySQL modules installed (or just install WampServer and get them all at once). I don't really want the responsibility of hosting it, either.

I'm in a bit of a hurry so I'm not posting a link to the code right now, but if there's interest (and someone knows a place I can drop it without requiring a sign-up) I'll put it up.

 

Features:

**Index**

----------

A link to the main DigiNotes page that has a list of all saved notes/books.

----------

**Left Nav Panel**

----------

All 'Chapter' headings are populated in this list, so it creates an automatic index of your notes.

----------

**Save Button**

----------

Saves the note to the database. A second tab is opened to verify that it saved properly. **Because the tab is opened before the save query is executed, you must refresh this tab to see your saved changes.** I typically save, then refresh to verify it saved, then close the extra tab. Also, you need to click on two elements after saving to reset the position indicator, because of the way the indexes are set up it needs a current and last element to set properly.

---------- **Position Div**

----------

A yellow bar indicating where the 'pointer' is in the document. Added elements get added below the yellow bar, and clicking the remove button removes the first element above the yellow bar.

----------

**Chapter**

----------

The highest level of headings. Links are created in the nav panel for all Chapter headings. Because DigiNotes was designed with taking notes from books in mind, I call it a chapter heading but you can easily change the text to anything you want.

----------

**Sub-heading 1**

----------

The 2nd heading level.

----------

**Sub-heading 2**

----------

The 3rd heading level.

----------

**List Title**

----------

The 4th heading level. Because of how it's formatted this works best for list titles, but these work great for creating nested lists.

----------

**Text**

----------

Creates a paragraph.

 

Limitations and issues:

 

* Formatting isn't preserved after editing. If you need formatted paragraphs create separate text elements for each paragraph. If you need other formatting use a picture or a table. * Bold and italic HTML tags work when entered but if the text element is edited then they get removed. * If a text element is being edited (it's focused) and another element gets added, the element gets added after the text element, not where the position div is. This has to do with how browsers handle 'focus' of the elements. * Really long strings (like links) overflow the editor area.

----------

Lists

----------

Creates a bullet list. Clicking on a list item will add an empty list element below the clicked element. If you don't need the extra element, just click on it to focus it then click elsewhere in the browser to take the focus away from it. Lists can't be nested.

----------

**Tables**

----------

Clicking the table button will pop up a dialog asking for the amount of columns and rows. The row and column headers **do not** count towards the number of rows and columns and are added automatically. I usually just edit the row headers to be blank if I don't need them. Note that if you edit them to be empty a hyphen is added. This gives you something to click on if you need to edit the header, because otherwise there'd be nothing to click on and the browser wouldn't be able to give it focus. Table sizes are fixed after being created, and the column width is rather small (though a simple CSS tweak would probably fix that).

----------

**Images**

----------

Images can be added through the image dialog (which must include the file extension), and any image that is supported by your browser should work (including gifs, though I haven't tested them). Images should be a maximum width of about 1000 pixels (unless you edit the CSS to make the editor wider).

----------

**Line Break**

----------

Adds an empty element that takes up space, used simply for adding space between paragraphs.

----------

**Remove Button**

----------

Removes the first element above the yellow position div. **Do not try to use the backspace button for removing an element, it'll just take the browser back to the previous page and will lose any unsaved progress**.

----------

**Other Limitations and Issues**

----------

* Elements can be inserted and removed in any order, but there's no way to sort them after they've been entered (besides copying and pasting the text into a new element). * The title can't be removed or edited (unless you edit the MySQL database). * Removing all elements will prevent you from adding another one (because adding elements requires a reference point). Admittedly, this would be a pretty easy fix but it's not really an issue for me so I've left it for now. * Books that aren't saved will show up on the Index page but the contents will be empty. * There's no math formula support, but a LaTeX to image converter will do the trick. * The editor has a fixed width of about 1000-1200 pixels. Like I said, it's my first web project and it was pretty much designed with my screen in mind, so if you're screen is wider either edit the CSS or give me a shout and I'll look into it.

----------

**Things I'd Like to Add**

----------

* Keyboard shortcuts * Export to PDF (as it stands it's not at all printer-friendly) * Sub-headings in the note's nav panel
